source_supported_findings.title: ALPS startup and pipe completion are not bounded or observed completely
source_supported_findings.cause: The blocking stderr readiness iterator precedes the 90 s process wait. A live silent child can therefore wait forever in direct capture. Stderr is drained by an unretained daemon whose print list-comprehension also retains one None entry per line until EOF; stdout reader join has a 10 s timeout but neither liveness nor thread failures are checked before rendering output. Finally kills/joins the process but does not join both pipe readers or close their streams.
source_supported_findings.contract: Acquire child ownership immediately, bound readiness and completion, and refuse success-shaped partial output after a failed or unfinished reader.
source_supported_findings.proposed_control: Use the actual capture entry with a real small child that signals startup ownership but stays silent, and a separate literal-listening/normal-exit positive. Capture finite deadline and joined child/reader termination. Inject a distinguishable pipe-read exception separately from actual OS faults; it must survive publication cleanup.
source_supported_findings.limits: No live subprocess reproduction. run_matrix has an outer finite process-container timeout, so this is a direct-tool/local ownership gap rather than an assertion that scheduled jobs run forever.

source_supported_findings.title: The first HTTP2 capture listener is not retained if second startup fails
source_supported_findings.cause: start acquires the TLS server, awaits plaintext startup, and only then assigns self.servers. run installs its finally after start returns. Second-bind failure or cancellation leaves the first acquired listener outside explicit close ownership.
source_supported_findings.contract: Retain each acquired listener before the next fallible/awaiting step and close all acquired listeners after startup failure while preserving the startup cause.
source_supported_findings.proposed_control: Occupy the requested plaintext port with an independently retained real loopback listener. Observe the actual first TLS listener acquisition through the start_server seam, then require typed second-bind failure and reacquisition of the observed first address while the runtime remains live. Preserve healthy two-listener traffic as a positive.
source_supported_findings.limits: No measured leaked socket. This TCP two-listener path is distinct from the already repaired A99 QUIC startup path.

source_supported_findings.title: Accepted callback completion and failures are outside capture ownership
source_supported_findings.cause: Servers retain writers, not the coroutine tasks created by asyncio.start_server. aborting writers and awaiting listener closure does not collect those callback Results. Hint/SSE respond or parse failures therefore go to the event-loop callback failure path rather than the run result; callers wait for done and may receive a timeout instead. HTTP2 records exception class deliberately, but still does not await callback completion before returning/moving to the next run.
source_supported_findings.contract: Capture owns accepted operations through error/cancellation/cleanup; explicit finish observes their completed outcomes and guarantees callbacks stop mutating returned records before publication. Preserve intentional partial-record policy explicitly.
source_supported_findings.proposed_control: After a literal GET and real response/body, hold the canonical handler at a controlled barrier with a retained peer/runtime. Cancel/close its capture owner, observe handler destruction before backup cleanup, and separately inject a typed completed respond failure that must be retained with any primary capture failure. No sleep readiness or permanent-leak oracle.
source_supported_findings.limits: Source only. CPython 3.10 creates callback tasks internally and listener wait_closed returns once the listener is closed; this does not establish a permanent socket leak. The 3.12 active-connection wait differs and was inspected only as an incidental qualification.

source_supported_findings.title: TLS application failures are rendered as clean EOF
source_supported_findings.cause: TlsChannel.read catches every ssl.SSLError alongside SSLZeroReturnError and taps empty data. The outer handler sees successful completion, so record.failure remains absent and client_eof is set for fatal TLS read errors. PlainChannel similarly collapses ConnectionError to EOF without distinguishing a reset from graceful closure.
source_supported_findings.contract: Distinguish clean closure/explicit expected peer departure from unrelated TLS/transport failures in retained evidence; preserve bounded non-sensitive failure context.
source_supported_findings.proposed_control: Complete a real TLS/request exchange first, then feed a deliberately invalid authenticated-record path or inject an explicitly labelled distinct SSL read failure at the canonical channel seam. Require failure evidence and no clean-EOF-only classification; healthy close_notify/ordinary peer-disconnect controls remain separate.
source_supported_findings.limits: No native SSL failure or OS reset reproduced. Generic connection resets may be legitimate peer departure, so their exact retained classification needs a deliberate contract rather than blanket rethrow/suppression.

source_supported_findings.title: Offline HTTP2/TLS helpers have unchecked bounds and malformed-success cases
source_supported_findings.cause: ClientHello indexes vector lengths before checking remaining bytes and length-prefixed strings accept short slices. Empty PADDED payload and short PRIORITY cause IndexError; excessive padding can silently produce an empty block. The analyzer does not verify CONTINUATION stream identity or required sequencing, overwrites pending HEADERS, and returns trailing=0/no block when a complete HEADERS frame lacks END_HEADERS. SETTINGS remainder is ignored and short GOAWAY fields become success-shaped zero values.
source_supported_findings.contract: Diagnostic decoders must reject malformed/truncated fields explicitly or retain explicit incomplete/invalid state. They must not silently assign a continuation to the wrong stream or present omitted incomplete blocks as complete analysis.
source_supported_findings.proposed_control: Call actual helpers with independently encoded minimal frame/vector bytes: complete HEADERS without END_HEADERS, wrong-stream continuation, short padding/priority, invalid padding length, partial settings/goaway and truncated ClientHello vectors. Preserve a literal valid multi-read/multi-frame ordered HPACK block positive. No duplicate parser to compute expectations.
source_supported_findings.limits: Source-only proof of branches, not a tested exhaustive RFC validator or a production client parser defect. Live h2 engine can separately mark protocol failure; raw offline consumers still have their own evidence contract. Python integers cannot overflow like the Rust capture parsers, and the HPACK continuation loop already has a finite shift guard.

source_supported_findings.title: Accepted IPv6 loopback addresses form invalid unbracketed URLs
source_supported_findings.cause: ipaddress accepts ::1 loopback, but the first/page/plain/socket URLs interpolate host:port without IPv6 brackets. This produces authorities such as http://::1:port, which do not represent the accepted endpoint.
source_supported_findings.contract: Every accepted address family yields a syntactically valid URL for the bound endpoint, or the unsupported family is rejected before acquisition.
source_supported_findings.proposed_control: Use the real server URL functions with a concrete observed IPv6 loopback address and parse the emitted authority using the standard URL parser; add actual loopback traffic where the integration host supports IPv6. Keep IPv4 literal positives.
source_supported_findings.limits: No IPv6 socket or browser execution here; no universal host IPv6 availability claim.

source_supported_findings.title: Capture argument/schema validation is incomplete
source_supported_findings.cause: Client-hint names are only checked for lowercasing/comma/ordinary space, so CR/LF/tab/colon values can reach the response header renderer despite the lowercase-field-name contract. Timeout/observation float arguments accept non-finite values without validation, allowing the promised finite wait to become unbounded. Fixture metadata is interpolated without single-line validation, while the atomic writer deliberately writes raw ASCII bytes.
source_supported_findings.contract: Validate actual field-name tokens, finite time units and single-line metadata before emitting wire bytes or a machine-readable fixture. Keep valid current literal metadata and hint values unchanged.
source_supported_findings.proposed_control: Invoke the real argument/render seams with independently literal invalid field tokens, infinity/NaN and metadata CR/LF, paired with ordinary lowercase token/finite timeout/literal metadata positives. These are configuration/schema controls, not a remote exploit claim.
source_supported_findings.limits: Source-only absence of validation; no native timeout behavior measurement. User-supplied metadata/options are not inferred secret material.

source_supported_findings.title: NetLog origin attribution uses substring membership
source_supported_findings.cause: HOSTNAME in origin/url admits a lookalike host or an unrelated URL query/path containing the target hostname. Such events are included in the target-origin restart evidence.
source_supported_findings.contract: Only the parsed intended origin/hostname belongs to the target evidence; unrelated source IDs or paths must not substitute for actual target requests.
source_supported_findings.proposed_control: Use netlog_lines with literal valid target events and independently unrelated https://other.test/?server.phantom.test plus https://server.phantom.test.other/. Require exclusion without weakening current target restart/field-order positive.
source_supported_findings.limits: No actual browser false attribution reproduced. Fresh launch DNS restrictions reduce unrelated activity but do not make the parser membership rule exact.

source_supported_findings.title: Scripted test clients can lose acquired ownership or supersede cleanup causes
source_supported_findings.cause: Client-hints fetch closes its acquired writer only on success; scripted context awaits its task without cancellation/finite join after primary exit. ScriptedH2.open acquires writer/pump before a fallible settings wait but has no internal startup cleanup. close can return on a completed pump error before closing the writer; the driver sequential loop then skips another acquired client. Unexpected cleanup can replace the primary exception.
source_supported_findings.contract: Test helpers preserve concrete primary plus cleanup causes and own acquired writers/tasks on setup, operation and cancellation failures. Local asyncio.run teardown is a distinct fallback, not observed helper cleanup.
source_supported_findings.proposed_control: After an actual loopback request/response or settings barrier, inject a distinguishable completed pump/setup failure, preserve live runtime/writer observations, and require finite cleanup for every acquired client. Positive exact capture/wire tests stay unchanged.
source_supported_findings.limits: No measured native leak or hanging test. Existing scripted WebSocket reset/error paths have deliberate limited peer-close suppression; its exact policy needs source-aware controls rather than blanket removal.

source_supported_findings.title: Independent guards and observation checks share dense paragraphs
source_supported_findings.cause: The hint decoder joins missing-colon validation, name conversion, credential validation and publication without paragraph boundaries. derived_hints joins input absence, per-run completion, reference selection, independent first/second comparison, duplicate validation and default-value/order checks. CLI independent guards similarly run together.
source_supported_findings.contract: Group preparation, independent validation, conversion and output by their actual responsibility; do not add a new module or helper solely to meet a line quota.
source_supported_findings.proposed_control: Manual source/diff and exact nonblank-token preservation check only for a later pure grouping change. No tests that mirror whitespace.
source_supported_findings.limits: Readability source finding, not a formatter failure or runtime defect. Imports/constants already have appropriate groups; no global formatting churn requested.

qualified_or_rejected_candidates.disposition: The tool records browser-reported outcome separately and verifies outgoing send policy against retained corpus indices. It does not claim a full echo-payload/server conformance suite; a count alone is not broader parity evidence, but no new route/client defect is established.
Intentional partial diagnostic evidence: capture_scenario records timed_out and result counts. Do not reclassify all partial publication as success-oracle failure.

standards_assessment: Manual lifecycle/input/error/responsibility/grouping review. Imports and constants in the five owner scripts follow standard/external/local grouping; domain names and section flow are clear. No generic framework, compatibility shim, arbitrary module split or performance claim. The missing ownership/error branches are actionable source findings, not scan counts.
independent_test_contracts: Current tests use literal NetLog restart/field sequences, two actual navigations with agreement/default-value/order checks, decoded HPACK representation/order/priority, actual rejected/refused H2 wire codes, exact outgoing corpus indices/lengths/compression/Close placement, SSE literal committed IDs/reconnect targets/probe-cookie policy/finite termination. These strong ordinary oracles must remain; they do not cover every new failure-path candidate.
limits: Source findings are not runtime reproductions. No measured browser parity, credential exposure, permanent leak, performance or whole-audit closure.
Every supporting read has its own partial/full classification. No complete browser launcher, snapshot, cookie capture or matrix audit from these ranges.
